label: copy phase: last/second-to-last output at recall position 3-4 (end of short sequences)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (100% of mass), concentrated at the final two copy steps (to_go 0-1 hold ~90% of mass) and at recall positions 3-4 (~89% of mass), so it is strongest for L=5 (t=9, final output) and L=4-6. Never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on the first copy steps (recall 0-1), and very rarely at to_go >= 4. Largest activations are on the last output step of L=5 sequences (e.g. t x c s h <DEL> t x c [s]), with a weaker activation on the step before. Within this positional window, firing is strongly but diffusely token-modulated: higher for some output tokens (h, r, d, f, p) and some inputs (a, v, t, s, c), and lower when there are many digits; no simple token set captures it, so precision is only ~0.43.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: a, s, t, v, c, q; least: g, 0, r, h) and the token being output (most: h, r, d, m, p, f; least: y, v, q, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=4, to_go=1, L=5 & t=9.
